newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Telrad buys more Koor shares.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Telrad buys more Koor shares.

text.p: Telrad Holdings Ltd said on Sunday it bought 60,000 shares of Koor Industries Ltd last week, representing 0.4 percent of the voting rights in Koor.
Telrad, a wholly owned subsidiary of Koor, paid 18.5 million shekels or 299.90 shekels per share. Koor is trading at 300.65 shekels a share.
The off-the-floor transaction was done through the Koor Capital Markets brokerage firm.
Telrad now controls 131,344 shares or 0.87 percent of the voting rights in Koor.
Telrad announced last month it would buy a further $10 million of Koor shares after buying $4 million worth.
Israeli companies are prohibited by law from buying their own shares but subsidiaries may buy shares in parent companies.
